description.narrative: The strategy of research and documentation is integral to the learning and evidence building agenda of the WGG Consortium and its country-level strategic partners. There are significant programmatic components of the consortium wide joint activities as part of global and regional advocacy efforts.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

1. Comprehensive Inclusion Guideline to ensure accessible, safe, and respectful spaces for all. It outlined inclusive policies emphasising privacy, consent, flexible leave, mental health support, and DEI-focused HR practices. It also provided needs-based support through accessible infrastructure, clear communication, interpreters, and assistance such as childcare or transport. Additionally, the guideline promoted comfort by respecting diverse identities, offering prayer and rest spaces, diverse dietary options, and fostering awareness on cultural, social, and gender issues. 2. SRHR One-pager to disseminate the research findings on the sexual and reproductive health realities of Dalit women. The one-pager included the research process, findings, and recommendations both from the field study and the validation workshops highlighting the existing limited SRHR knowledge and low uptake on SRHR services, economic and gender dependency, cost and access barriers, and intersecting marginalisation in the community, following the recommendations including community-based workshops, training Dalit women as peer educators on SRHR, active monitoring of the existing health centres engaging local authorities, and strengthening links between Dalit women and government and NGO-run clinics to ensure free or low-cost SRHR services.
